demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- AI client initiatives are shifting from pilots to production-scale deployment, with demand concentrated around data monetization, workflow automation, and embedding AI agents into existing applications; individual deal sizes remain small to moderate, but engagement volume per client is rising
- Cybersecurity is moving to the center of client budgets as cloud adoption, AI agent deployment, and machine-identity growth expand the attack surface; identity and access governance for autonomous AI agents is an emerging specific area of demand
- Clients continue to move AI-native workloads to production cloud environments, with IaaS/PaaS leading demand; Global Capability Centres have expanded beyond back-office functions into product engineering, AI, and platform ownership
- RPA remains a steady base, but client interest is consolidating around hyperautomation and agentic orchestration combining automation, AI, and analytics
- AI-driven productivity gains are pushing clients toward outcome-based and consumption-based pricing in place of traditional time-and-materials models
- Elevated geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty may prompt clients to defer or reduce spending on non-essential IT initiatives

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- distribution: presence balanced across India, the Middle East, and the US, each contributing meaningfully to revenue — evidence: chairman states 'businesses in the Middle East and the United States gathered real momentum' and 'each now contributes meaningfully rather than aspirationally'
- technology: process discipline behind AI system build/evaluation extended from its formal quality accreditation — evidence: 'We have extended the process discipline behind our CMMI Level 3 assessment into how we build and evaluate AI systems'

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Pursuing strategic initiatives through both organic and inorganic growth
- Reskilling programs to move employees into newer technologies and methodologies
- Differentiating through specialized capabilities and deeper client relationships rather than price alone
- Proactively developing outcome-based and value-based pricing frameworks ahead of client demand
- Diminishing concentration risk by growing across regions, clients, and industries, supported by a diversified technology and geography mix
- Building AI governance, data engineering, and AI-enablement services as a distinct client offering
- Focus on cost-optimization and vendor-consolidation offerings to support clients managing uncertain discretionary budgets
